headline: NWS confidence grows for late-week coastal storm in southern New England
dek: Forecasters say gale-force winds are increasingly likely over southern waters Friday night into Saturday, with storm-force gusts and coastal flooding or erosion possible as the storm track takes shape.
body: The National Weather Service Boston/Norton office said Wednesday morning that confidence is increasing in an impactful coastal storm for Friday into the weekend. The immediate forecast remains dry, cool and breezy through Thursday, while Gale Warnings continue for southern coastal waters.

Forecasters say a low-pressure system could slowly move north and retrograde west into waters south of Block Island and Nantucket. The exact track remains uncertain, but the strongest winds could arrive as early as Friday evening or as late as Saturday afternoon.

The office says gale-force winds of at least 34 knots, or about 40 mph, are becoming increasingly likely across southern waters, with storm-force winds near 48 knots, or about 55 mph, possible Friday night into Saturday. The system could also bring rain and build rough seas across the region.

A prolonged period of northeasterly wind would raise the risk of coastal flooding and erosion, especially along east-facing beaches and harbors. The latest guidance identifies Nantucket Harbor as having the greatest risk for at least minor flooding around high-tide cycles Friday, Friday night and Saturday.

The National Weather Service said no additional weather headlines were being issued yet, and the storm’s track and strength will determine how far inland rain and damaging winds reach. Residents, boaters and coastal businesses should monitor updated forecasts as the system develops.
author: NorthEast News Desk
